title: Quant profiles pipeline: CI calibration + accuracy regression gate for weight-only INT8 (GPTQ/AWQ)
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Purpose: Add a reproducible CI pipeline that runs weight-only INT8 quantization (GPTQ and AWQ variants) calibration and accuracy validation for served models. The pipeline should produce artifacts (quant profiles, calibration logs, accuracy diffs) and gate merges when accuracy regressions exceed thresholds. This ticket coordinates the engineering work to integrate the calibration runner, standardize datasets and prompt sets, define accuracy gates, and hook results into PR checks and a nightly regression job.
acceptance_criteria: A CI job exists that runs weight-only INT8 quantization (both GPTQ and AWQ codepaths) for targeted model families and emits a quant profile artifact
Calibration runner accepts a dataset identifier and outputs per-layer scales and summary metrics; artifacts uploaded to build storage
Accuracy validation runs a fixed prompt/eval set and reports metrics (perplexity/accuracy/embedding-cosine) and a delta relative to FP16 baseline
PR gate blocks merges if any model-profile pair exceeds the configured accuracy delta thresholds (configurable per-model-family)
Nightly full regression runs across the model catalog and posts a dashboard with trend lines and failing profiles
Fallback policy implemented: on significant regression, release automation pins the PR to use FP16 fallback and flags for a manual review
test_plan: Add unit tests for the calibration runner's serialization of quant profiles
Add end-to-end CI job that runs on a small model (e.g., small-7b) to validate pipeline wiring
Nightly job runs on larger models (13B/70B family) on a limited subset of prompts
Create a synthetic adversarial prompt set to surface edge-case regression for attention-sensitive layers
Compare logits/ppl and normalized embedding cosine similarity against FP16 baseline; define gating thresholds (e.g., <= 1.5% relative ppl increase OR embedding cosine >= 0.985)
Verify artifacts stored at gs://redwood-quant-artifacts/<run-id> and links appear in PR check output

tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Start with weight-only quant profiles (no activation quant) to reduce functional risk and speed calibration. This minimizes regression surface but yields smaller compression gains than full int8 activation+weight quantization.

Tradeoff: AWQ tends to be faster to apply in the runtime but occasionally shows slightly larger accuracy variance on small datasets. We'll gate both algorithms separately and allow runtime routing by user policy.
Decision: Use a hybrid metric gate (ppl delta + embedding cosine) instead of single metric to reduce false positives for classification vs generation workloads.
Tradeoff: Nightly full-run on 70B models is expensive. We'll keep nightly runs to a sampled prompt set and run a weekly deep pass for critical models.
Decision: Artifacts will include both raw quant profile and a compact telemetry summary to minimize storage and ease quick triage. Full logs kept for 30 days; summaries persisted longer.

notes: Calibration runner currently supports per-channel and per-tensor scaling. We chose per-channel for GPTQ and AWQ as default for better layer sensitivity.
We will version quant profile schema as v1.0 with fields: model_id, algorithm, layer_stats[], global_seed, dataset_id, commit_hash, tool_version.
CI gating thresholds are configurable via a repo-level YAML: .ci/quant-gates.yaml
Add an opt-out label 'skip-quant-ci' for performance-heavy PRs to speed iteration during local experiments (this should be used sparingly and audited)
